description:
## Scope

Workspace-architectural sweep derived from review findings:

- bd:JMAP-ayoz.33 (metadata-server review) — 'memory.rs query_objects uses unchecked as casts between usize/u64/i64'
- bd:JMAP-x2gd.53-companion (chat-server review, per workspace memory) — same finding at chat-server scope

Every extension-server MemoryBackend's query_objects / query_changes / max-cap check uses 'as' casts across signed/unsigned/width boundaries:

```rust
let total = ids.len() as u64;                              // usize -> u64
let start = if position >= 0 {
    (position as usize).min(ids.len())                     // i64  -> usize
} else {
    let neg = position.saturating_neg() as usize;          // i64  -> usize
    ids.len().saturating_sub(neg)
};
ids = ids[start..]
    .iter()
    .take(limit.map_or(usize::MAX, |n| n as usize))        // u64  -> usize
    .cloned()
    .collect();
Ok(QueryResult::new(ids, start as u64, ...))               // usize -> u64

if relevant.len() as u64 > max { ... }                     // usize -> u64
```

## What can go wrong

- **u64 -> usize on 32-bit targets**: a request with limit > 4GB elements silently truncates. Theoretical for in-memory demo backends; real for production backends cookie-cut from the same template.
- **i64 -> usize negative cast**: position.saturating_neg() pivots i64::MIN to i64::MAX, then 'as usize' is target-dependent.
- **usize -> u64 widening**: safe on 64-bit targets, but clippy::cast_lossless prefers From::from.

## Per-crate cast site counts (as of 2026-05-16)

| Crate | 'as' cast sites |
|---|---|
| jmap-mail-server (canonical) | 51 |
| jmap-chat-server | 12 |
| jmap-calendars-server | 10 |
| jmap-tasks-server | 9 |
| jmap-contacts-server | 9 |
| jmap-sharing-server | 9 |
| jmap-metadata-server | 9 |
| jmap-filenode-server | 5 |

**Total ~114 sites.** Per-crate audit needs to separate query/limit-path casts (in scope, vulnerable to truncation) from other 'as' uses (e.g., serialise width helpers, hash mixing) which may be intentional.

## Decision: fix shape

Per bead .33's recommendations:

- **u64 -> usize**: `usize::try_from(n).unwrap_or(usize::MAX)` — caps at architecture limit.
- **i64 -> usize**: explicit guard `if n < 0 { 0 } else { usize::try_from(n).unwrap_or(usize::MAX) }`.
- **usize -> u64**: idiomatic `u64::try_from(n).unwrap_or(u64::MAX)` OR `n as u64` with clippy::cast_lossless escape hatch (safe widening on supported targets).
- Pattern: prefer explicit guard + try_from; widening casts can stay 'as' if a doc comment notes they are platform-safe.

## Canonical-first per workspace AGENTS.md

jmap-mail-server is the canonical extension-server template. Fix lands there FIRST (51 sites), then 7 siblings propagate (.2-.8). Each sibling bead blocks on .1.

## Per-crate children

1. **Canonical:** jmap-mail-server (51 sites)
2. jmap-chat-server (12 sites)
3. jmap-calendars-server (10 sites)
4. jmap-tasks-server (9 sites)
5. jmap-contacts-server (9 sites)
6. jmap-sharing-server (9 sites)
7. jmap-metadata-server (9 sites)
8. jmap-filenode-server (5 sites)

Each child:
- Audits its sites to separate query/limit-path casts from intentional/safe 'as' uses
- Replaces query/limit-path casts with explicit guards + try_from per the shape above
- Adds inline comments on any 'as' that remains, citing the platform-safety reason
- Adds at least one negative test (e.g. position = i64::MIN doesn't panic; limit = u64::MAX caps to usize::MAX, not 0)
- cargo clippy -- -D warnings green WITH clippy::cast_possible_truncation / clippy::cast_lossless lints enabled crate-locally (optional but recommended)

## Why P3

Clippy-priority, no behaviour change on 64-bit targets where the workspace currently ships. Real bug surface is 32-bit targets which the workspace does not currently support.

## Acceptance

- All 8 child beads closed
- Workspace-wide grep for the specific query/limit-path 'as' anti-pattern returns zero results
- Each in-scope cast site replaced or annotated
- Workspace test suite green
- Per-crate negative tests added

## Cross-references

- Triggering: bd:JMAP-ayoz.33, bd:JMAP-x2gd.53-companion
- Sibling sweep epic for HashMap allocation: bd:JMAP-grs0 (option (a) nested HashMap, also workspace-cookie-cut from x2gd.52 — same epic pattern)
title: Workspace sweep: unchecked 'as' casts in *-server MemoryBackend query/limit paths
